headline: NO FOOT-OF-PAGE APPARATUS ON ANY OF THE SIX PAGES, on either witness -- a checked zero, consistent with the three pages already recorded for this work. ONE [sic:] is fireable and fired (0381B, two witnesses). SEVEN defects found, ALL of them Corpus Corporum's, filed as TEI patches. structural_finding: THE TWO COPIES OF PL 113 ARE TWO PRINTINGS, NOT TWO PHOTOGRAPHS, in this range as in 8950's. Five sites differ in a way ink cannot produce: 0384C lumbos (Gallica, = our twin, = Pr 30:31) against archive lumbo; 0384C amieos (Gallica, = our twin) against archive amicos; 0384D dexteram (Gallica, = our twin) against archive dextram; 0386A the LEMMA 'Applica tribum' (Gallica, = our twin, = Nm 3:6) against archive 'Accipe tribum' -- a whole word; 0387D 'Jesus Christi' (Gallica, = our twin) against archive 'Jesu Christi'. In this range OUR TWIN FOLLOWS THE GALLICA PRINTING at every one of the five. ⚑ That has a consequence for the stint's own apparatus: at 0384C the reading our twin carries (amieos, Jo 15:15) is a NON-WORD that only ONE printing has, so it may not take a [sic:] -- the two-witness bar for accusing Migne's type is not met when the two witnesses disagree. It is rendered by sense (friends) with a crux and no marker. ⚑ The archive copy is again the worse witness here: 9 archive-only readings refuted against 0 confirmed.

reads.found: Corner numbers 381/382 both copies. No foot-of-page apparatus, either copy. CONFIRMED ON BOTH WITNESSES, and it is the stint's one [sic:]: 0381B prints, in italic, the un-construable abbreviated run 'ne temporis re. p. t.' after 'deinde praecepit', with the column anchor falling inside it. Four archive-only candidates, ALL REFUTED BY GALLICA, our twin right at each: 'Cauta omnia provisa' (Gallica and twin: Caute); 'Licer Numeri appellatur' (Gallica and twin: Liber); 'poctores gentium' (Gallica and twin: doctores); 'Decima, ctc.' (Gallica and twin: etc.). Latin twin's '[n: (RAB. in Num. )]' carries a stray space before the paren that the plate does not; too small to patch, recorded only.

Corner numbers 383/384 both copies. No foot-of-page apparatus, either copy. THREE defects CONFIRMED ON BOTH WITNESSES as OUR TWIN'S, all filed as TEI patches: 0383C plate 'cupiunt', twin 'eupiunt'; 0383D plate 'ut acci-piat' broken at the line end, twin 'acci piat' (a de-hyphenation failure, Pattern 10 shape but NOT Migne's); 0384D plate 'VERS. 39.', twin 'VERS. 59.' -- the archive digit is unambiguous at 600 dpi and Gallica agrees, and Nm 1:39 (Dan, 62,700) is the verse 'Septingenti' belongs to. Three press variants here (lumbos/lumbo, amieos/amicos, dexteram/dextram) -- see structural_finding; no marker, no patch.

Corner numbers 385/386 both copies. No foot-of-page apparatus, either copy. ONE defect CONFIRMED ON BOTH WITNESSES as OUR TWIN'S: 0386D plate 'Alienati sunt peccatores a vulva', twin 'Alicnati' -- a non-word, and the same clause prints correctly nine lines above in the twin itself. TEI patch filed. Three archive-only candidates, ALL REFUTED BY GALLICA, our twin right at each: 'Quid ad sacrum ministerium indignus accedit' (Gallica and twin: Qui); 'de illis Israel' (Gallica and twin: de illis filiis Israel); and the archive's lemma 'Accipe tribum' at 0386A, which is a press variant rather than ink -- Gallica, our twin and Nm 3:6 all read 'Applica tribum'. ⚑ Calibration note for anyone reading this leaf: on the Gallica scan the printed digit 3 renders very like a 5 at 1400px (its 'VERS. 5. -- Sacerdotum' is Nm 3:3 and its 'quaest. 5' is Augustine's quaest. 3); every digit call in this stint was therefore settled on the archive copy at 600 dpi with Gallica used only to corroborate.

Corner numbers 387/388 both copies. No foot-of-page apparatus, either copy. NO defect attributable to either party. Two archive-only candidates, BOTH REFUTED BY GALLICA, our twin right at each: 0388A archive 'impendere. ub Eleazaro, Sid est Dei adjutorio' -- a displaced S that reads exactly like the 8955 'ulit/Tulit' broken sort, and Gallica prints 'Sub Eleazaro, id est Dei adjutorio' cleanly; 0388C archive 'ne otiosus et inutilis adjiciatur' (Gallica and twin: abjiciatur). One press variant at 0387D (Jesus/Jesu Christi) -- see structural_finding. Migne's 'Quatuor fili Aaron' at 0386A-0387A stands on both copies and is the ordinary medieval -ii > -i contraction, Pattern 9: no marker.

Corner numbers 389/390 both copies. No foot-of-page apparatus, either copy.
